questions.prompt: Ten parallel iterations update the same key. What does this print?
options: A value below 10 that varies between runs
questions.explanation: `AddOrUpdate` is an atomic add-or-update: the first call inserts 1 and every later call applies `old + 1`, so after 10 iterations the value is 10.
`ConcurrentStack<T>` is LIFO: `TryPop` removes the top item, which is the last one pushed (2).

questions.prompt: A `BlockingCollection<int>` was created with `boundedCapacity: 3` and already holds 3 items. What happens when the producer calls `Add(4)`?
options: It throws because the collection is full
It drops the oldest item to make room
It blocks until the consumer removes an item, then adds 4
It returns `false` and the producer moves on
questions.explanation: When the collection reaches its bound, the next `Add` blocks until space becomes available; once the consumer takes an item, the blocked `Add(4)` completes.

source.section: #### 2️⃣ What happens when producer and consumer run

questions.prompt: A consumer loops with `foreach (var item in bc.GetConsumingEnumerable())`. When does that loop end?
options: As soon as the collection is momentarily empty
After `CompleteAdding()` has been called and the collection is empty
When the bounded capacity is reached
Never; you must break out of it manually
questions.explanation: `GetConsumingEnumerable()` iterates until the collection is completed: it stops when `CompleteAdding` has been called and no items remain.

questions.prompt: Which concurrent collection keeps a local store per thread and may "steal" items from another thread's store in `TryTake`?
questions.explanation: Only `ConcurrentBag<T>` has a per-thread local bag: `TryTake` looks in the current thread's bag first and steals from another thread's if it's empty. The others are single shared structures.
